unresolved_should_improve.claim: The revision deletes the condolence letter from King at Pasadena. It then quotes King's 'waiting' phrase with no source and follows with 'impressed him', where the nearest male referent is King rather than Hay.
unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: The paragraph opens on Hay, and the lament's 'sickened me to witness it' implies an observer other than King. Most readers will recover the attribution.

evidence.quote: Among the letters of condolence showered upon him was one
Among the letters of condolence was one from Clarence King at Pasadena
Clarence King was "simply waiting till nature and the foe have done their struggle." The tragedy of King impressed him intensely.

unresolved_should_improve.minimal_repair: Restore the first draft's letter-of-condolence sentence, or write 'The tragedy of King impressed Hay intensely.'
unresolved_should_improve.plan_relation: Required (continuity check on Hay attribution); the minor quoted phrases are optional.
unresolved_should_improve.reader_effect: The reader loses how King enters Hay's grief and the 'old King manner' that echoes the earlier portrait. The plan's check that the lament is attributed to Hay is weakened at the moment it matters.
unresolved_should_improve.title: King's condolence letter cut, leaving his words unframed and 'him' ambiguous

unresolved_should_improve.claim: The revision cuts three things. The first is the geometrical-demonstration sentence that gave 'this' a referent. The second is the claim that the political machinery of great countries supplied the best information. The third is Adams's concession that he had mechanical certainty about Coal-powers and Gun-powers. All three survived in the first draft.
unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: V6 and V7 survive, and the Czar/Kaiser/Mikado closing still lands.

unresolved_should_improve.minimal_repair: Restore the first draft's 'machinery of politics' sentence and its 'mechanical assurance ... Coal-powers ... Gun-powers' sentence, with 'Even so' before the Czar clause.
unresolved_should_improve.plan_relation: Required (the final reversal is essential); the source's paragraph 17 is only optionally compressible.
unresolved_should_improve.reader_effect: Adams's ignorance is shocking because knowledge, information and mechanics were all at their peak. Without these premises the turn to ignorance reads as an assertion rather than an earned paradox. 'This was the moment' and 'these two minds' also lose clear anchors.
unresolved_should_improve.title: Final reversal loses its 'maximum information' and 'mechanical assurance' premises

unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: Paragraph 10's 'but he was not a Senator' still implies the contrast with Lodge.

evidence.quote: but Roosevelt and Lodge were playing a game in which they were always
Roosevelt and Lodge were always liable to find the shifty sands of American opinion yield suddenly under their feet.
Double standards are inspiration to men of letters, but they are apt to be fatal to politicians. In domestic politics the larger study was lost in the ambitions of fifth-rate men.

unresolved_should_improve.minimal_repair: Reinstate the first draft's 'shifty sands' sentence after the maxim.
unresolved_should_improve.plan_relation: Required (essential: 'Double standards are fatal to politicians').
unresolved_should_improve.reader_effect: The 'but he was not a Senator' payoff and the Lodge portrait lose their consequence. The paragraph's argumentative hinge, from Bostonian double standards to political danger, becomes an orphaned epigram.
unresolved_should_improve.title: 'Fatal to politicians' no longer applied to Roosevelt and Lodge

unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: Paragraph 4 still separates Hay's half-gladness from Adams's pure loss.

Even Hay's relation was a false one, while Adams's ceased of itself.

unresolved_should_improve.minimal_repair: Restore both clauses from the first draft; together they add about 20 words.
